narrative:
The model estimates an 82% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system has learned from many similar employee profiles.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, the time you have spent in your current organization, and the fact that you have received other job offers while working here. 

Your total professional experience of 6-10 years pushed the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, half had only 1-5 years of experience, so your longer track record made you appear more likely to move on. Similarly, having spent 1-5 years in this organization also increased the likelihood of departure; this tenure is actually the most common range among those predicted to stay, yet in your specific combination of circumstances it still contributed to the “will leave” direction. Finally, receiving external job opportunities was a clear push toward leaving. Only 23% of employees predicted to stay had received such offers, making this one of the strongest signals that you may be considering options elsewhere.

Taken together, these elements created a profile the model associates with higher turnover risk. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly, while you may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term plans. Addressing these points early could change the outlook for both sides. (248 words)
